newsitem.title: USA: China to need 20 MMT grain imports by 2000 - Study.
newsitem.headline: China to need 20 MMT grain imports by 2000 - Study.

text.p: China's grain import needs will gallop in coming years, reaching 20 million tonnes at the end of this decade, but will not create chaos in world food supplies or prices, a think tank reported Monday.
The report by International Food Policy Research Institute said domestic production in China also would rise, dampening the need for imports.

"It appears that China will neither empty the world grain markets nor become a major grain exporter," it said. "It does seem likely, however, China will become a more important player in world grain markets as an importer in coming decades. Both potential exporters outside of China and those charged with managing China's food needs through domestic production and imports need to be ready. Exporting countrie --especially those dealing with wheat and maize -- will undoubtedly be the beneficiaries of these trends in the short run."
Australia, Canada and the United States would be among the exporters to benefit from larger imports, said Mark Rosegrant, co-author of the report.
Also writing the report were Jikun Huang, director of the Center for Chinese Agricultural Policy in Beijing, and Scott Rozelle, assistant professor at Stanford University.

"In recent years, China has responded with investments in agriculture as they are needed to increase productivity," said Jikun. "Our baseline projections of grain output are far below the more optimistic estimates givne in recent years fy Ministry of Agriculture officials but the gap between production and demand won't be large enough to trigger the world food crisis that some observers fear."

Increased demand for meat will drive the need for larger grain supplies, the report stated. Chinese consumers were projected to more than double their consumption of fish, meat and poultry from 19 kgs in 1991 to 43 kgs per person in 2020.
The report estimated 38 percent of grain would be fed to animals in 2020, compared to 20 percent in 1990.
At the same time, less grain would be eaten as food. Rice consumption per capita would drop by 10 percent.
With high population growth, imports would be 52 million tonnes in 2020 -- still not so large to cause a global crisis.
